thread:
Tariq: FYI — partner reseller BrightLayer flagged an overcharge for their end-customer (neo-apps). They were billed $6,200 in burst on top of a 4-GPU reserved commit. BrightLayer insists traffic stayed flat. Invoice INV-20260602 attached. Can billing check commit attribution?

Maya: Linking the usage export now: s3://billing-exports/brightlayer/neo-apps/2026-06.csv. Do we show the requests coming from the reseller gateway or direct customer tokens?

billing-bot: Export ready — brightlayer/neo-apps/2026-06.csv. Summary: total tokens 520M, burst tokens 62M, burst charges $6,200. BILL-3325 opened to track.

Owen: Quick check: many burst rows have metadata source="reseller-gw" and partner_id=bright-22. But a subset (~18%) has source="thirdparty-integration" and tag="vendor_integrated_model" which bills at on-demand premium.

Tariq: BrightLayer says their integration should be routed through our partner reserved pool. If some traffic hit on-demand because of mis-tagging that's on us. Can we map request_id -> pool id?

Maya: Running a join to pool_allocations table. Found ~11k requests on 2026-06-02 14:40-15:05 UTC routed to pool_id=ondemand-pool-3. Pool had capacity reported OK, so suspect a labeling error in gateway that sent header X-rlw-mode=external causing routing rules to treat it as external.

Owen: Also noticed many requests include header "X-Reseller-Partner: bright-22" but missing "X-Reseller-Commit: 4g". Our router prefers explicit commit headers. If gateway omitted it, the request fell back to on-demand.

Tariq: Action items: 1) Generate corrected usage where requests with partner header but missing commit are attributed to partner commit pool; 2) Contact BrightLayer to confirm gateway config; 3) Provisional credit until final reconciliation.

Maya: I'll create corrected CSV (attribute by partner header) and calculate differential between billed on-demand and partner-rate. ETA 4 hours.

billing-bot: BILL-3325 updated: provisional credit hold requested.

Owen: Quick calc: differential for the affected tokens = $4,120. If we add a small goodwill credit for partner ops friction say $500, total credit = $4,620. Recommend provisional credit $4,620 while we validate gateway logs.

Tariq: Approve provisional credit up to $5,000 for BrightLayer to keep partner happy. Maya — please attach corrected export and routing evidence so Finance can finalize.

Maya: Corrected export posted s3://billing-exports/brightlayer/neo-apps/corrections/2026-06-attrib.csv. Notes: ~11,480 requests re-attributed; partner header present but missing commit in 100% of re-attributed rows. Differential computed = $4,120.

billing-bot: Provisional credit $4,620 applied to INV-20260602. Notification sent to brightlayer-account. Support ticket #4740 linked.

Owen: Also filed INF-7915 for router to accept partner header as fallback when explicit commit header missing. PM task PM-1041 added to update integration docs.

Tariq: BrightLayer replied: "Thanks for quick resolution. We'll patch our gateway to include commit header in next deploy." They requested a short note for procurement confirming credit applied.

Maya: Finance — please finalize credit of $4,620 and close BILL-3325 once docs attached. I'm marking rows as partner_attributed in billing pipeline to prevent double-billing on next run.

Tariq: Approved. Closing after Finance confirms final credit.

billing-bot: BILL-3325 closed. Final credit $4,620 applied to INV-20260602. Artifacts: s3://billing-exports/brightlayer/neo-apps/corrections/2026-06-attrib.csv.

Owen: Added post-mortem note: ensure router fallback for reseller header and add alert on high mismatch between partner header and commit header. PM-1041 tracking.

Tariq: Good work. Partner happy, procurement unblocked.

Maya: Closing thread.
